// FIXTURE - the shape the guard must stay silent about. Stored as .cs.txt so
// it is never compiled.
//
// Two things are proven here:
//   1. Raw process starts that are NOT a coding-agent CLI (git, verification
//      commands) remain legal - the guard centralises CLI invocation, it does
//      not ban Process.Start.
//   2. A CLI binary name mentioned only inside a comment is not a violation.
//      Historical note: this file used to call Process.Start with
//      FileName = "claude" and RUNNER_CLI_ARGS. It no longer does.
using System.Diagnostics;

namespace AgentRunner;

internal static class CompliantExecution
{
    // Git plumbing keeps its own spawner; the CAR migration does not touch it.
    public static Process Git(string repoPath, params string[] arguments)
    {
        var psi = new ProcessStartInfo
        {
            FileName = "git",
            WorkingDirectory = repoPath,
            RedirectStandardOutput = true,
            UseShellExecute = false,
        };
        foreach (var argument in arguments) psi.ArgumentList.Add(argument);
        return Process.Start(psi)
            ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("failed to start git");
    }

    // The coding-agent CLI goes through the execution layer, never through a
    // process start assembled here.
    public static Task<CliRunHandle> RunAgentAsync(
        ICliDriver driver,
        CliRunRequest request,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
        => driver.StartAsync(request, cancellationToken);
}
